claim: The torus spectral solve reproduces the dense torus KRR solution to 2.3e-12 relative inf-norm (both kernels, 32x32, lambda 1e-3) -- exact FOR THE EMBEDDED-TORUS KERNEL, with spectral floor and free-boundary gap disclosed.
The free-boundary modeling gap is measured and shrinks with resolution: relative max-alpha gap matern32 1.74 (32x32) -> 1.12 (72x36) -> 0.31 (144x72); rbf 0.43 -> 0.57 -> 0.37.

Full-field torus spectral masked-pixel reconstruction RMSE 0.071 (matern32) / ~0.32 (rbf) with split-conformal coverage 0.88-0.91 (mean 0.901, field std 0.021, n=48) at target 0.90: calibrated but halo_w2 (0.881) below target -- not uniformly achieved.

Genuinely masked-input training (exact free-boundary PCG) converges to tol 1e-8 (final rel residual 5e-9..8e-9, 420-550 iters) at masked-input RMSE 0.78-0.83 -- ~11x the full-field reconstruction cost; quantified cost of missing inputs.

Kernel-consistent Nino3.4 functional RMSE 0.0628 is a SMALL (~6%) gain over the zero-model ablation 0.0665, both far below climatology 0.993 and the RBF direct head 1.009 (~16x better) -- gain framed modestly.
Cross-month stationary-kernel pooling baselines do not transfer (RMSE 1.25-1.27, ~field std) -- informative negative; per-field parity measured separately.

FFT-KRR resource accounting is first-class: total wall-clock 70.8 s (12 cores) under the 90-min cap; sub-ms fits to N=10,368; O(N) memory ~42 MB peak estimated at 0.25-deg global, far below the 7 GB cap; every artifact records wall_clock_s/peak_rss_gb/estimated_flops/estimated_bytes.

RBF torus Gram at 36x72 has negative eigenvalues (min -3.5e-4); spectral floor applied; floor-eps sensitivity measured: masked RMSE 0.0945 at eps 0/1e-8/1e-6, 0.089 at 1e-4, 0.011 at 1e-2 (over-floored) -- insensitive for eps<=1e-6.

All results are synthetic-from-physics [simulated]; every artifact carries dataset.origin + simulation_marker; claims scoped to algorithmic properties and relative-method comparisons; real-data external validation is roadmaped via scripts/convert_netcdf4.py (h5py converter, not executed on this stack).

This is an engineering/evaluation integration over established FFT-kernel methods (Gray 2006; Dietrich-Newsam 1997; Wilson-Nickisch 2015): the concrete circulant-block CPU implementation + systematic exact-vs-randomized benchmark + leakage-aware CV protocol + resource accounting on climate grids. No newness claimed for FFT kernels.
